channel.title: The GATAS Lab | GATAS Lab
channel.description: The GATAS (Generalized Algebraic Techniques Advancing Science) Lab at the University of Florida uses applied category theory to develop novel approaches to scientific computing.

item.title: Members
item.description: The members of the lab come from diverse perspectives with unique training. We are always looking for students and researchers with a desire to solve problems by leveraging abstract applications in novel science and engineering applications. We are hiring The lab is accepting PhD students, postdocs, research scientists, and undergraduate researchers. See how to join for what we are looking for and how to get in touch.

item.title: Join the Lab
item.description: The lab is a mix of backgrounds – dynamics and control, high-performance computing, category theory, programming languages – pointed at one problem: making scientific models composable enough to build out of parts instead of from scratch. We are always looking for students and researchers who want to work on that, whatever they trained in. Lab dinner at Cry Baby’s Tyler Hanks’s PhD hooding Teaching diagrammatic reasoning in the lab A first Gators football tailgate Watching the Gators win the 2025 basketball national championship The last ASKEM hackathon, on top of a mountain Benjamin Merlin Bumpus summons a presheaf A tour of HiPerGator, the university’s supercomputer Tea in Oxford, during the ACT conference A visit to the whiteboard that turned into InterTypes.jl We are accepting applications for PhD students in both MAE and CISE. Mathematically minded students would benefit from the MAE degree program specializing in Dynamics, Systems, and Control. For MAE applicants, the lab is particularly well suited to students interested in either Dynamics, Systems, and Control for optimization and dynamics projects or Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) for the Decapodes project. For CISE students, the lab is a good fit for students interested in High Performance Computing (HPC), Machine Learning, Data Science, Applied and Computational Mathematics, Computer Algebra, and Programming Language Theory. Research projects for undergraduates and graduate students in MAE, CISE, and Math. Research scientists and postdocs in MAE, CISE, and Math. What the work looks like Most of what we do ends up as software. Every project on the research page is a line of papers and a Julia package in the AlgebraicJulia ecosystem, written with Evan Patterson’s group at the Topos Institute and used by people outside the lab. That means the mathematics has to be right and the code has to run, and lab members spend their time on both.

item.title: Research
item.description: We work in a small number of long-running projects, each with its own papers, software and people. The projects are the place to start; the lists that follow are the record. Everything here is generated from the same Zotero library, so the tables, the bibliography and the talks list always agree with each other. item.title: Software
item.description: Much of our research is released as software. These packages are open source and developed in collaboration with the AlgebraicJulia team, including Evan Patterson’s group at the Topos Institute. The names on each card are the lab members, past and present, who work on it. Decapodes.jl Compose and simulate multiphysics systems from diagrams of PDEs. item.title: Lab Meetings
item.description: Each week the GATAS Lab holds a lab meeting where one or two lab members gives a 30-60 minute presentation. We use these presentations for practice talks or educating each other on open problems. Here you can find a collection of previous talks. item.title: 8th International Conference on Applied Category Theory
item.description: About The 8th International Conference on Applied Category Theory (ACT) took place together at the University of Florida on June 2-6, 2025. The conferences were preceded by the Adjoint School on May 26-30, 2025. For more information on the ACT series, see here. This conference has taken place ACT 2025 was held at the University of Florida on June 2-6, 2025.
